title: Courage Is a Command
scripture_text: Haven't I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don't be afraid. Don't be dismayed, for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.
body:
Joshua was taking over from Moses. Moses, who had parted a sea. Every person Joshua was about to lead had spent forty years watching someone else do the job he was now expected to do.

God tells him to be courageous three times in nine verses. You do not repeat yourself to someone who is already fine.

What is strange is that courage is given as a command. We usually treat bravery as a temperament — some people have it, most of us watch them. But a command implies it is something you can obey whether or not you feel it. Courage here is not the absence of fear; it is moving anyway, because of a fact you have decided to believe: your God is with you wherever you go.

Notice the reason God gives. Not "because you are ready." Not "because it will work out." Because I am with you. The courage is borrowed. It always was.

There is something this week you have been putting off because you are afraid of it — a conversation, an apology, an honest answer. You will probably still be afraid when you do it. Do it afraid.
discussion_questions: What have you been avoiding because you are afraid of it?
How is courage different from confidence?
What changes if 'God is with you' is a fact rather than a feeling?
activity: Name the thing you have been avoiding. Do one step of it today — even just sending the first message.
